name: PalmClaw
vibe_summary: An academic-grade (EMNLP 2026 demo) OpenClaw-inspired agent framework that runs natively on Android phones with no PC required. It keeps the full agent loop, memory, and skills on-device while delegating inference to a user-configured LLM API.
best_for: Users who want an agent running natively on an Android phone
Researchers evaluating mobile on-device agent architectures
Developers building mobile-first agent tools without a PC/server
avoid_if: You need a desktop or server-based agent runtime
You want a large plugin/skills ecosystem like OpenClaw's
You need production stability beyond an early v0.3.x release
openclaw_advantages: Runs natively on Android with no PC or server required
Structured mobile device tools with permissions and confirmations
Academic backing with a published paper and 769 tests
Simple APK install path for non-technical users
openclaw_disadvantages: Much smaller community and ecosystem (1.1k stars vs OpenClaw's scale)
Still requires a cloud LLM API for inference
Early-stage v0.3.x maturity with limited channel integrations
AGPL-3.0 license is more restrictive than OpenClaw's MIT
confidence_summary: README and commit evidence is solid for architecture and activity, but community sentiment is weak — all 13 Reddit matches are unrelated (mouse grip discussions), so real user feedback is essentially absent.

overview_markdown:
PalmClaw is an open-source AI agent framework inspired by OpenClaw, built specifically to run natively on Android phones without requiring a separate PC or server. Presented as an EMNLP 2026 demo with an accompanying arXiv paper, it keeps sessions, context management, memory, skills, tools, and the agent loop entirely on-device, while model inference is delegated to a user-configured LLM API endpoint.

Architecturally, it is written in Kotlin and distributed as a ready-to-install APK, exposing mobile capabilities through structured device tools governed by schemas, permissions, confirmations, and workspace boundaries. Recent commits show active hardening of the MCP client lifecycle, provider endpoint compatibility, and always-on channel reliability, backed by a reported 769 tests — unusual rigor for a project at v0.3.1.

Compared to OpenClaw, PalmClaw trades ecosystem breadth and multi-channel reach for true mobile-native operation: there is no desktop runtime, no Linux container, and no server component. Its main limitations are the continued dependence on a cloud LLM for inference, an emerging rather than mature skills ecosystem, and a more restrictive AGPL-3.0 license.
